# v1.1.0-dev.127: Custom resolutions for every display, dialogs that fit, and a UX pass

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.126`. Nine
commits: one feature, a sizing pass over every dialog, and the fixes
from a UX and accessibility audit of every screen.

## Custom resolutions

- Custom resolutions are a list that every display's picker offers,
  marked `(custom)`, the moment you add one. They used to exist only for
  a virtual display whose driver WLM could write to, and only after a
  registry write, an administrator prompt and a reconnect.
- Registering a size with a virtual display driver is now an optional
  tick per row in the same dialog, shown when one display is selected
  and a writable driver is behind it. Sizes already in the registry are
  folded into the list.
- A custom size the display does not offer yet gets the same "not
  offered yet" badge and next step a by-hand value does.

## Dialogs and the window

- Dialogs are fixed-size, fitted to their content and capped at 90% of
  the app window. They scroll only when that cap is what sized them.
- The app window opens at 1280 by 720 by default. Settings > Display
  has a "Reset window to default size" button for when it has wandered.
- The Display dialog is 760 wide instead of 900 and draws the monitors
  larger. Settings is 900 wide instead of 1040, and every tab is one
  column.
- The companion scan shows a spinner while its rows are still the
  catalog's guess rather than what winget found.

## From the UX audit

- **Update is now Re-capture.** The profile action that replaces a
  profile's saved windows with the ones open now is called Re-capture
  on the button, in the palette, the confirm and the key hints. "Update"
  meant three things at once. The `u` key is unchanged.
- Dim text, the Delete button and the visual editor's desktop tags all
  reach the WCAG AA contrast floor. Dim text is a little brighter
  everywhere as a result.
- Every Settings help paragraph is one or two lines that say what the
  control changes, with the reasons under a "Why?" you can open.
- The footer's coffee button is an outline, so Load is the one filled
  button on the main screen. Delete sits a gap away from Rename and
  Duplicate. Uninstall on a companion card is a text button.
- Keyboard focus is visible on the two main panes and the Settings
  tabs. Command palette rows are one line each. The smallest pills and
  badges are 11px instead of 10. The Display chip reads "Display: off"
  rather than a dash.
- Virtual Windows is marked Beta everywhere the app names it.

## Under the hood

- A cleanup pass removed dead symbols and two unused Win32 bindings, and
  the crash box no longer says "startup error" an hour after startup.
- `npm test` now checks the contrast of the text tokens from the
  stylesheet, and the stylesheet's spacing values against its own scale.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
